chosen.premise: Two Pokédex entries say Zapdos appears only when a thundercloud splits into two halves.
chosen.hook: Zapdos has a bizarre entrance requirement: split the thundercloud.
chosen.visualIdea: A dark thundercloud tears cleanly into two halves, revealing Zapdos between them.
chosen.note: Exceptionally concrete and strange, with the same claim repeated in two entries. The only slight weakness is that the visual can imply a literal rule more strongly than the wording’s “said to appear” phrasing.

candidates.premise: Two Pokédex entries say Zapdos appears only when a thundercloud splits into two halves.
candidates.hook: Zapdos has a bizarre entrance requirement: split the thundercloud.
candidates.visualIdea: A dark thundercloud tears cleanly into two halves, revealing Zapdos between them.
candidates.note: Exceptionally concrete and strange, with the same claim repeated in two entries. The only slight weakness is that the visual can imply a literal rule more strongly than the wording’s “said to appear” phrasing.

candidates.premise: Zapdos gains power when lightning strikes it, turning the attack into its own recharge.
candidates.hook: What if getting struck by lightning made Zapdos stronger?
candidates.visualIdea: Lightning hits Zapdos, then an energy meter visibly rises instead of falling.
candidates.note: A strong Zapdos-specific contradiction with an instantly understandable visual. The Pokédex explicitly says lightning increases its power, though “recharge” is a useful metaphor rather than the source’s exact wording.

candidates.premise: Galarian Zapdos keeps the same 1.6-meter height but is 5.6 kilograms heavier and loses Electric typing.
candidates.hook: Same height, different type—and Galarian Zapdos weighs 5.6 kilos more.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen compares identical height bars, a heavier weight readout, and Electric/Fighting type swaps.
candidates.note: Every comparison is directly supported and highly visual. It is a strong variant-comparison episode, but the numerical weight change is less inherently dramatic than Zapdos’s unusual lore mechanics.

candidates.premise: Zapdos’s glittering wingbeats are said to create savage thunderstorms, making flight itself destructive.
candidates.hook: For Zapdos, flapping its wings can create a savage thunderstorm.
candidates.visualIdea: Each wingbeat transforms a clear sky into darker clouds, rain, and branching lightning.
candidates.note: Repeatedly supported and easy to animate, but the broad storm-causing premise is less novel than the lightning-strike contradiction or split-cloud entrance.

candidates.premise: According to Shield, Zapdos can make lightning fall immediately by rubbing its feathers together.
candidates.hook: Zapdos only has to rub its feathers together to summon lightning.
candidates.visualIdea: Close-up feathers scrape together, followed instantly by a lightning bolt hitting the ground.
candidates.note: Very filmable and specific, but it relies on one Pokédex entry and may overstate the action as a deliberate summon rather than a reported sequence.

rejected.reason: hook: Too big: expected string to have <=80 characters

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; this choice would be strengthened by showing the exact Pokédex wording on screen and framing “recharge” as an interpretation of “gains power,” not a literal game mechanic.
